newsitem.title: USA: SBC asks court to overturn FCC phone charge rules.
newsitem.headline: SBC asks court to overturn FCC phone charge rules.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc said Tuesday it asked a U.S. appeals court to overturn key aspects of landmark federal rules overhauling the nation's complex web of domestic phone charges.
The San Antonio, Texas-based Baby Bell also said it would ask the St. Louis-based court to suspend the Federal Communications Commission rules while judges consider the carrier's request.
SBC earlier this month asked the FCC to stay its rules, saying they would put the carrier at a competitive disadvantage and that some customers could face rate hikes.

In particular, the carrier said the FCC went too far in ordering an immediate $1.7 billion reduction in the access charges long-distance carriers pay to connect to the local phone network. SBC also complained that the FCC rules would permit competitors to lease parts of the local network without having to pay access charges.
The FCC is not expected to grant the stay. SBC's court challenge deals with the same issues.

"We now must appeal to the courts in order to protect universal service and the interests of our customers, employees and shareholders and to preserve a level playing field for competitors in today's telecommunications industry," SBC Senior Vice President Zeke Robertson said in a statement.
"The FCC must find a fair and effective way to distribute the burdens and obligations of protecting affordable phone service for all Americans."
MCI Communications Corp has asked a U.S. appeals court here to overturn the access-charge rules, saying the FCC did not go far enough in ordering reductions.
